title: Trump Tariff Turmoil, Private Credit Risk Grows, & AI’s Software Fears | The Weekly Wrap
summary: Eisman treats tariff policy as disruptive but unlikely by itself to overwhelm US resilience. His main concerns are AI capital returns, software-heavy private credit and insurance links. He distinguishes payment-network moats from exposed software, remains skeptical of solar and Warner Bros valuation, and finds Netflix more interesting. Nvidia and Circle operating growth is supported, while Circle reserve interest is dominant rather than its sole revenue. Private-credit transaction ownership, insurance leverage and loss forecasts require further primary verification.
assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman is the sole substantive speaker; viewer questions are distinguished from his responses.
framework_points: Focus on growth, funding and related-party incentives across private credit and life insurance.
Use network effects to distinguish payments from software-disruption fears.
Separate reported earnings strength from market narrative and valuation.
Recognize that institutional information advantages do not guarantee outperformance.
tools_and_charts: Private-credit fund discounts and redemption restrictions
transcript_cautions: Montage repeats the later qualified UBS default scenario; Eisman expressly says he does not know whether 15% is realistic.
Kuvare Asset Management ownership is not automatically ownership or legal control of Kuvare Insurance.
Viewer GDP/PCE figures are not silently attributed to Eisman.

claims.claim: The Supreme Court invalidated tariffs imposed under IEEPA; replacement Section 122 and Section 301 actions create uncertainty but might preserve tariff revenue.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare actual court scope, replacement authority and customs receipts with an unchanged-policy counterfactual.
claims.reason: The IEEPA ruling is verified; the projected fiscal neutrality of replacement measures is not established by that judgment.

evidence.title: Learning Resources v Trump opinion
evidence.publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
evidence.finding: Court holds IEEPA does not authorize presidential tariffs; it does not invalidate every tariff authority.
